newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bank derivatives holdings up $782 bln in Q3.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bank derivatives holdings up $782 bln in Q3.

text.p: U.S banks increased their holdings of off-balance sheet derivatives by $782 billion, or four percent, to $19.8 trillion in notional value in the third quarter, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corp reported Friday.

The biggest increase was in interest rate and foreign currency swaps. At the end of the third quarter, banks held $6.8 trillion in interest rates swaps, up from $6.3 trillion at the end of the second quarter, and $433 billion of forex swaps, up from $410 billion, FDIC said.
Holdings of exchange-traded interest rate contracts were almost unchanged, rising to $3.39 billion from $3.37 billion.
Holdings of forex futures and forwards rose to $4.8 trillion from $4.7 trillion.
Option contracts grew modestly, although an increase in interest rate option contracts masked a decline in forex option contracts.

Interest rate option holdings totaled $3.1 trillion at the end of the third quarter, up from $2.9 trillion at the end of the second quarter. Forex option holdings totaled $974 billion, down from $1.06 trillion.

derivatives declined to 501 from 507 the previous quarter. While the notional values provide a measure of derivatives activity, the figures do not indicate the value of derivatives assets or liabilities for banks.

The replacment value of bank derivatives, a measure of the current market value of the positions, rose slightly to $199 billion from $193 billion at the end of the previous quarter but still well below the $219 billion level seen at the end of 1995, FDIC reported.
and forex contracts covered by risk-based-capital standards, FDIC said. Futures contracts are not included.
Replacement values also excluded forex contracts with a maturity of less than 14 days, FDIC said.

The derivatives market remained highly concentrated among a few banks, the FDIC said. The eight largest banks reporting derivatives held $18.6 trillion, or 94 percent, of the total. The other 493 banks held $1.3 trillion.

Commodity and equity derivatives continued to make up a tiny portion of the market, each totaling about $200 billion notional. Interest rate derivatives accounted for $13.3 trillion and forex for $6.2 trillion.

Most off-balance sheet derivatives, about $18.3 trillion, were held in trading accounts where they are regularly marked to market, FDIC said. About $1.6 trillion was not held for trading, FDIC said. ((-- Aaron Pressman, 202-898-8312)) (c) Reuters Limited 1996
